text:
elaine: posted overnight perf run for the mid-priority cluster. p99 balloons when we hit GPU util > 82% AND kv-miss rate > 28%. curious if microbatch sizing or kernel choice is amplifying the tail.

samir: can you paste the profiler snapshot?

elaine: sure, here's the condensed tail section from the profiler:

```
# sample window: 90s
requests: 12k
gpu_util: 79-88%
microbatch_size median: 12
microbatch_size p90: 24
kv_miss_rate: 5% -> 32% (correlated with spikes)
p50: 32ms p95: 78ms p99: 310ms (during peaks)
kernel: mix of fused-attn / fallback-unfused after kvcache thrash
queueing_delay spike aligned with kvmiss bursts
```

priya: wow p99 310ms is rough. Looks like when KV misses spike the runtime flips kernel to unfused path which increases per-token cost and also prevents batching coalescing.

ben: is the kernel flip immediate? we have hysteresis on kernel picker right?

elaine: it's tied to sequence-length distribution + kv cache hit inference. the fallback is triggered when mem overhead > threshold and then async memcpy adds ~30-40ms per request in some cases. combined with larger microbatches it amplifies tail.

samir: I'd propose a two-pronged tweak: 1) add a short-duration KV-miss detector that lowers target microbatch cap for the next N windows, 2) keep kernel picker from switching to unfused unless sustained for M seconds. basically reduce headroom when kvmiss rises.

priya: agree. suggestion for config:

```
{"kv_miss_watch_ms": 1500,
 "kvmiss_rate_threshold_pct": 20,
 "microbatch_max_default": 32,
 "microbatch_max_kvmiss_mode": 8,
 "kernel_hysteresis_secs": 6}
```

ben: note: lowering microbatch cap helps latency but increases GPU inefficiency. we need to simulate cost impact vs p99 improvement. can we run a targeted canary with production distribution?

elaine: I ran a small sim against replayed traces. quick numbers:

```
baseline (microbatch_max=32): p99=310ms, throughput=100k tokens/s, cost_index=1.0
kvmiss-mode (max=8): p99=120ms, throughput=78k tokens/s, cost_index=1.12
kernel-hyst-only: p99=210ms, throughput=95k tokens/s, cost_index=1.03
```

samir: so tradeoff looks reasonable: 60% p99 reduction for ~12% cost increase in worst case. That seems OK for mid-priority workloads with strict latency SLO.

priya: any risk of oscillation? if we drop microbatch and kv hit recovers, we should ramp back quickly to regain efficiency. we need ramp-up policy to avoid slow drift.

ben: implement add-back ramp: increase microbatch cap by +2 every 2s until default. and revert kernel picker hysteresis after 3s of stable low kvmiss. keep safety upper bound to avoid overshoot.

ops-bot: @ops-bot NOTICE: scheduled canary run for cluster mid-priority at 03:00 UTC with kvmiss-mode enabled & kernel-hyst=6s.

elaine: i'll own telemetry: compare p50/p95/p99, kvmiss, gpu_util, tokens/s, and kernel-switch events. will post summary in morning.

samir: one more thought — admission control: if gpu_util > 90% AND p99 trending up, trigger light shedding for best-effort classes to restore headroom. we should not rely solely on microbatching.

priya: agreed. combine both: fast local microbatch cap adjust + slow cluster-level admission when util > 90% for 5s.

ben: SGTM. please add a short playbook snippet for oncall so they know what to expect. elaine, can you draft?

elaine: will do. draft playbook:

```
1) alert fires: p99 > 200ms && kvmiss_rate > 20% for 30s
2) check canary state (kv-mode on?)
3) if canary off, enable kvmiss-mode on affected pool
4) if gpu_util > 90% and p99 still high -> enable admission-shed for best-effort routes
5) if p99 recovers -> disable admission-shed, ramp microbatch cap back gradually
6) if not recovered in 10min -> page runtime-eng oncall
```

samir: perfect. thanks team. looking forward to the morning report. :coffee:

elaine: thanks — will follow up with logs and flipped-kernel timestamps.

ben: thumbs up :thumbsup:
